transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-02-18 15:00 PST — Duration 58 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood), Marta Ruiz (HeliosWave), Derek O'Neal (HeliosWave), Samir Patel (HeliosWave), Lina Park (HeliosWave)

Summary (auto): quick intro, partner GTM options, technical constraints, next steps captured.

00:00 Alex Chen: Hey everyone thanks for taking the time, um this is Alex from Redwood inference, I'll do a 5 minute intro then pass to Priya to run through a quick infra map and questions.
00:12 Marta Ruiz: Hi thanks Alex, excited to chat. We're in partnerships at HeliosWave so wanted to see what collaboration modes are possible.
00:20 Alex Chen: Great, quick context on Redwood - dev-first inference platform, we do Hosted API, Dedicated reserved GPU pools, and Private VPC/on-prem installs. We focus on predictable latency and cost controls, so yeah tradeoffs are latency vs cost and control.
00:35 Derek O'Neal: Cool. On our side we operate a channel and cloud reseller business, we also run a small managed service — some customers need on-prem. Our question: what integration pattern would you prefer for partners? marketplace listing vs direct reseller/onramp?
00:52 Priya Nair: Hi Derek, Priya here. From a technical POV there's two common patterns we see: 1) Marketplace/reseller where HeliosWave resells Redwood host capacity — quick to market but less control for end-customer on data residency. 2) Private/dedicated onramp where Redwood ships a private control-plane + runtime that you can run in customer VPCs or on-prem — more work but required for regulated customers.
01:15 Samir Patel: That private control-plane: is it full on-prem or hybrid? How's the networking look — we run transit VPCs and have strict egress rules.
01:26 Priya Nair: It's flexible. We can do private control plane with customer-managed networking, and we support an on-prem bundle for air-gapped setups. Typical pattern is customer VPC peering or private link into Redwood-managed infra for hosted control plane. For on-prem, we provide deployment artifacts and ops docs. There are also options for using customer KMS/HSM for keys.
01:47 Lina Park: Security is big for us. SOC2? ISO? And are audit logs available for end-customers — HeliosWave needs to demonstrate supplier SOC2 to our enterprise accounts.
01:58 Alex Chen: Redwood is SOC2 compliant (Type II). We can share our attestation and an overview of our audit logs and RBAC model. We also integrate with SSO (SAML/SCIM) and support KMS integrations. I'll add that to the artifacts we'll send.
02:10 Marta Ruiz: From GTM perspective we need clear commercial tiers. Do you support partner-led billing? Referral? Reseller retainer?
02:20 Alex Chen: All of the above — we've done partner-led reseller agreements and marketplace listings. For reseller we can enable partner invoicing and a rev-share model. We'll send sample templates.
02:30 Derek O'Neal: On the technical side — what about latency sensitive workloads; we have customers in fintech that need sub-200ms P95 for short prompts. How does Redwood handle that on your Dedicated offering?
02:44 Priya Nair: Dedicated gives predictable throughput; we allocate reserved GPU pools, autoscaling policies. For sub-200ms you'd want to pin to low-latency variants, smaller seq lengths, and possibly quantized kernels. We also do prefix/KV cache to reduce repeated token cost and latency on chat-style sessions. We'll want to benchmark with your typical prompts to validate.
03:05 Samir Patel: Benchmarks — good. We have an internal fleet of A100s and some customers want inference on L40s too. How does model routing across GPU types work?
03:18 Priya Nair: Our runtime has smart routing: it picks compatible model variants and kernels based on hardware. If L40 isn't supported for a quant variant, we can fall back to a compatible variant — with routing policies by latency/cost/region. It isn't magic but we've tuned it for common infra.
03:34 Marta Ruiz: Do you provide a partner API or white-label endpoints so HeliosWave can present a single branded endpoint to customers?
03:43 Alex Chen: We support partner-level tokenization and can issue partner tokens; white-labeling is possible for Dedicated/Private — hosted API is more standardized but the fronting can be done by HeliosWave in the integration. We'll explore specifics in legal.
03:57 Derek O'Neal: Regarding pricing: are there commit levels for Dedicated? We want predictable margins.
04:05 Alex Chen: Dedicated is reserved capacity — monthly/annual commits with burst options. We can build a partner pricing sheet with suggested margins and recommended commit sizes based on your book of business.
04:18 Jordan Lee: (murmur) also see optimize toolkit, helps tune batching and quantization by workload.
04:25 Samir Patel: How much engineering effort for the private control plane? Our SI team will want an estimate.
04:33 Priya Nair: Typical onboarding has these phases: discovery & infra mapping (1 week), pilot config & small integration (2-4 weeks), pilot run & tuning (2-6 weeks), rollout. If you want an on-prem packaging we usually need 4-8 weeks to produce the artifacts and test in a lab. Complexity depends on SSO/KMS integration and custom network constraints.
04:56 Lina Park: Can you outline data retention / logs? Customers often want logs, but we need to ensure no PII is retained unless requested. Also encryption at rest/transport.
05:10 Priya Nair: We have token-level logs available in the console; retention is configurable and we can exclude sensitive fields. Encryption in transit is TLS; at rest we support customer-managed KMS for key control. Audit logs are available for admin actions.
05:26 Marta Ruiz: Pilot success criteria — what would you propose?
05:31 Alex Chen: For channel pilots we usually define: 1) functional parity vs baseline (accuracy/regressions), 2) latency & cost thresholds for target workflows, 3) integration completeness (SSO, billing, logging), 4) commercial sign-off. If these are green in a 30-60 day pilot we expand.
05:49 Derek O'Neal: On the commercial side, any minimum commit? We're used to minimums for Dedicated.
05:56 Alex Chen: Depends on the region and GPU type — we'll include examples. For many partners we do low-touch reseller options with zero commit and revenue share, and a Dedicated option with minimum commit tiers.
06:08 Samir Patel: A couple of technical Qs — how do you handle KV cache and multi-tenant isolation? If we're routing many customers through a shared pool how do you keep caches per-tenant?
06:22 Priya Nair: KV cache is per-session/per-container; we isolate via tenant IDs in the runtime and enforce memory quotas. If you want absolute isolation we recommend Dedicated pools or single-tenant Private installs. There's also continuous batching — we batch compatible requests but we segregate batches by policy so tenant data doesn't bleed into others.
06:43 Jordan Lee: note: sometimes transcriptions say K V cache spelled out weird.
06:48 Samir Patel: ha yes, sorry.
06:50 Marta Ruiz: Any concerns with marketplace listing — e.g., restricted models? Some of our customers ask for vetted models only.
06:58 Priya Nair: Our model catalog curates open models and we also provide verified performance profiles. Partners can choose which models to surface. For regulated customers we recommend Private deployments with pinned model versions.
07:14 Derek O'Neal: On auditing and compliance: can HeliosWave pull per-customer logs for billing and incident review?
07:23 Alex Chen: Yes, we can surface per-customer metrics and logs; for deeper audits we can provide exportable logs or integrate with SIEM via syslog/forwarder. We'll add an example integration doc.
07:36 Samir Patel: Network constraints — some customers only allow inbound from specific IP ranges, no egress to public. Any way to support that?
07:45 Priya Nair: Yes — Private installs or on-prem solves that. We can also use private link/VPC peering for hosted control-plane minimal egress. We'll want to capture your exact topology to recommend.
07:58 Marta Ruiz: Perfect. What does the partner onboarding look like from a sales motion view? Do we get co-selling materials, joint logos, case studies?
08:07 Alex Chen: We have a partner portal, joint marketing kits, and co-sell credits for qualified referrals. We typically do joint calls, co-branded decks, and case studies after successful pilots.
08:19 Derek O'Neal: Competitors question — some customers compare with CloudGiant AI which offers low price but weaker latency. How do we position Redwood?
08:27 Alex Chen: Positioning is production-first: reliable latency, predictable economics and the unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private. We also emphasize observability and rollout controls — canary deployments and automatic fallback.
08:43 Samir Patel: Regarding fallback: if a model variant is out of capacity does Redwood automatically fallback to a different region or variant? Any SLA implications?
08:52 Priya Nair: Yes, smart routing can fallback to compatible variants or regions; SLA depends on plan (Dedicated has stronger SLOs). We'll map fallback strategies in the architecture doc.
09:05 Marta Ruiz: Ok lets talk pilot scope briefly — HeliosWave would run an initial pilot with 2 customers: one cloud-native SaaS account and one regulated on-prem account. For the SaaS account, they want a hosted/reseller flow. For the regulated on-prem, we need Private.
09:25 Alex Chen: That aligns with our recommendations. For the SaaS one we can do reseller listing + partner tokens and a light integration. For the regulated one we'd propose a Private control-plane install in their VPC or on-prem bundle.
09:38 Derek O'Neal: Timeframes? We need something we can present to our board by early March.
09:45 Alex Chen: If we start next week, discovery + infra mapping in a week, pilot config in 2-4 weeks, pilot run 4-8 weeks — rough timeline could get you initial pilots in ~6-10 weeks. We can expedite if you prioritize.
09:58 Samir Patel: Any pre-requisites we should gather before the deep-dive?
10:03 Priya Nair: Yes please send network diagrams, GPU inventory, a representative prompt set, expected seq lengths, and compliance docs. Also a list of which customers for pilot and their requirements.
10:16 Marta Ruiz: We'll start collecting.
10:20 Alex Chen: Cool. Quick note on licensing — for Private we usually do platform licensing plus support tiers. We'll include an example.
10:29 Derek O'Neal: One more technical: inference engine — do you ship optimized kernels or rely on vendor libraries? Some of our infra partners manage their own kernel stack.
10:40 Priya Nair: We have a GPU-optimized inference engine with attention optimizations, selective kernels and quantization-friendly paths. We also support vendor libs where appropriate, but the runtime orchestrates kernel selection for perf.
10:55 Samir Patel: Good. Costs — how do you advise partners on cost allocation and margin?
11:03 Alex Chen: Our Optimize toolkit suggests batching, cache, and quantization profiles and we model per-token unit economics. For partners we provide a sample cost model so you can price with a margin on top.
11:16 Marta Ruiz: Great. Anything else from you Jordan?
11:20 Jordan Lee: no, just capture notes.
11:23 Lina Park: Security question — do you support customer-managed HSM for signing tokens and keys?
11:30 Priya Nair: Yes HSM/KMS integrations are supported for Private and can be integrated for Dedicated in some cases. We'll document supported KMS providers and recommended architecture.
11:42 Derek O'Neal: Ok sounds good — let's lock the deep-dive for Tues 2026-02-24 if that works.
11:50 Alex Chen: Works for us — Priya will take point on scheduling. We'll also send the partner deck, security pack, and the initial commercial template.
11:59 Marta Ruiz: Thanks everyone, excited to move forward.
12:04 Alex Chen: Thanks all, we'll follow up with action items.

End of transcript.
